text: For the linear first-order ODE y' + P(x) y = Q(x), the integrating factor is:
choices: e raised to the negative integral of P dx
e raised to the integral of Q dx
e raised to the integral of P dx
explanation: Multiplying by mu = exp(integral of P dx) makes the left side the exact derivative (mu*y)', so mu*y = integral of mu*Q dx. The exponent must be +integral of P (not negative), and it depends on P, the coefficient of y, not on the forcing term Q.
